tier_reason: The integer-compression-benchmarks README tables, run by the VTEnc author, compare VTEnc against Delta+FastPFor128/256, BinaryPacking, VariableByte and VarIntGB from Lemire's SIMDCompressionAndIntersection on an i7-6700HQ. The harness code is public (timestamps.cc, gov2.cc, common.cc on Google Benchmark), and the Makefiles give g++ -O3 -std=c++11 for the harness and gcc -O3 -march=native for VTEnc, but no compiler version is stated anywhere. That is first-party code with partial methodology, so C (same precedent as other entries missing a compiler version).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC, version not stated; harness Makefile: g++ -Wall -O3 -std=c++11; VTEnc Makefile: gcc -std=c99 -DNDEBUG -O3 -march=native -mtune=native; SIMDCompressionAndIntersection built with its own makefile; Google Benchmark v1.6.1 in CMake Release
corrections.caveats: Speed win holds only on the highly regular timestamp file (ts.txt). On gov2.sorted, VTEnc/1 is slower than every bit-packing and varint baseline but compresses best; only VTEnc/16+ approaches or beats FastPFor decode speed (VTEnc/16 829.11 M/s vs FastPFor256 621.17 M/s, at a slightly lower ratio of 6.10 vs 6.13), and Delta+BinaryPacking/VarIntGB remain faster. Speeds are bytes of uint32 input per second (Google Benchmark SetBytesProcessed), so the ts.txt encode at 102.28 G/s exceeds the laptop's memory bandwidth; VTEnc's bisection over sorted runs with many duplicates evidently skips most input, so this is an algorithmic effect specific to that data, not a general throughput figure (inference from the code, not stated by the author). The encode benchmark does not check output, though the decode benchmark checks equality after decoding. The author runs the shootout; numbers were taken with VTEnc v0.3.0 in 2022. The library is marked as early-stage with no format stability. Last commit 2022-12-01. Tangential to bit-packing, kept because it is compared directly to FastPFor/BinaryPacking/VByte.

notes: All claimed_speedup numbers match the integer-compression-benchmarks README tables.
